rule_summary: Foster carers (assistants familiaux) are salaried professionals. They need an approval (agrément) from the council of the département where they live.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. Approval is given by the council's maternal and child health service (PMI).

rule_summary: Carers work for the département or for an association that helps children. The employer, usually the council, signs a work contract with them.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. Most council pages say approval does not guarantee a job.

rule_summary: Foster carers (assistants familiaux) are not the same as adult carers (accueillants familiaux). Adult carers host older or disabled adults under a separate approval.
notes: Mayotte council page on adult carers. Service-public has a page on the difference.

rule_summary: Applicants must be French, citizens of the European Economic Area, or hold a residence permit that allows work.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: Applicants must not have been convicted of offences linked to children. The council obtains bulletin n°2 of the criminal record for adults in the home.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. Applicants cannot request bulletin n°2 themselves.

rule_summary: Carers need a valid certificate of good character (attestation d'honorabilité). It covers the carer, adults in the home and children over 13 who live there.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. Needed at first application, at renewal, when hired and when the employer asks.

rule_summary: The certificate of good character checks the criminal record and the sex and violent offenders register (FIJAISV). It has been compulsory for child welfare staff since October 2025.
notes: News item published 4 February 2026. It says a certificate arrives in about 15 days.

rule_summary: Applicants send a medical certificate showing their health allows them to care for children.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: The PMI service checks that the applicant speaks French well enough.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: The home must guarantee the safety, health and physical, intellectual and emotional development of the children.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: The PMI service studies the file, meets the applicant at least once and visits the home at least once. It uses a national grid of criteria.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: For a first application, national guidance recommends attending an information meeting run by the PMI service. Many councils make it compulsory.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. See the regional rows for councils that make it compulsory or optional.

rule_summary: The council must decide within 4 months of a complete file. If it does not reply in time, approval is granted.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: If the file is incomplete, the service asks for the missing items within 15 days.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: The approval states how many children the carer may look after at once. The limit is 3, unless an exception is granted.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. The limit includes young adults under 21.

rule_summary: Approval lasts 5 years.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: Carers who hold the State diploma for foster carers (DEAF) get an approval with no time limit.
notes: Stated on the Gironde council page and by several other councils. The national article was not read.

rule_summary: Carers must ask for renewal at least 3 months before approval ends. The council sends the form during the final year.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. Renewal follows the same steps as the first application.

rule_summary: Before the first child arrives, the carer must complete a preparatory course. The 2025 decree raised it from 60 to 100 hours.
legal_citation: Décret n° 2025-305 du 1er avril 2025; arrêté du 1er avril 2025
notes: News article by Banque des Territoires (Caisse des Dépôts). It says the decree applies to requests made 3 months after publication on 2 April 2025.

rule_summary: After the first work contract, carers follow training towards the State diploma (DEAF). It rose from 240 to 420 hours, over 18 to 36 months.
notes: Service-public confirms the 18 to 36 months and the four blocks of skills. The diploma moved to level 4.

rule_summary: Holders of some childcare and social work diplomas can have the diploma training shortened. They still take the preparatory course.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. The diplomas named are auxiliaire de puériculture, éducateur de jeunes enfants, éducateur spécialisé and puéricultrice.

rule_summary: Each département sets carer pay. For one child, pay must be at least the monthly minimum wage (SMIC), shown as €1,867.02 gross.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026. This is a salary, not a maintenance payment. A daily maintenance allowance is paid on top.

rule_summary: Each extra child adds at least 70 times the hourly minimum wage a month, shown as €861.70.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: Carers also get a daily maintenance allowance for each child. The minimum is 3.5 times the minimum guaranteed amount (minimum garanti).
notes: The €14.35 figure from 1 May 2023 is from a parliamentary answer seen in search results. The amount follows the minimum garanti.

rule_summary: The 2022 child protection law raised minimum pay to the SMIC from the first child. A decree of 31 August 2022 raised the minimum for extra children to match.
legal_citation: Loi n° 2022-140 du 7 février 2022; décret n° 2022-1198 du 31 août 2022
notes: Government answer in the Senate, published 13 October 2022. It says the rise was up to €277 net a month.

rule_summary: Since the 2022 law, carers get 80% of their contracted pay for each planned placement that does not happen because of the employer.
notes: Government answer in the Senate, published 13 October 2022.

rule_summary: Each carer must be part of a team of social, education, psychology and health professionals. The carer takes part in the child's plan (projet pour l'enfant).
notes: Added by the law of 7 February 2022, per the Senate answer.

rule_summary: Carers are salaried but are not civil servants. No national collective agreement covers the job. Most contracts end with one month's notice.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 1 June 2026.

rule_summary: Since 31 October 2026, public employees may also work as foster carers. They may care for only one school-age child or young adult under 21.
notes: News item published 9 November 2026. The employee must ask their employer in writing first.

rule_summary: An approval (agrément) is needed to adopt a ward of the State (pupille de l'État) or a child from abroad. It is not needed to adopt a partner's child.
legal_citation: Code civil art. 353; CASF L225-1 to L225-10
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: A person adopting alone must be over 26.
notes: Service-public page checked 13 May 2026. Search results say the law of 21 February 2022 lowered the age from 28.

rule_summary: A couple can adopt if both partners are at least 26, or if they have lived together for more than 1 year.
notes: Service-public page checked 8 June 2026.

rule_summary: Married couples, couples in a civil partnership (Pacs) and unmarried couples living together can adopt jointly.
notes: Search results say the law of 21 February 2022 opened joint adoption to Pacs and unmarried couples.

rule_summary: Couples who have lived together for more than 1 year can adopt whatever their age. They must prove how long they have lived together.
notes: Search results say the 2022 law cut this from 2 years.

rule_summary: A single person can adopt. If they are married or in a Pacs, their spouse or partner must consent.
notes: Service-public page checked 13 May 2026.

rule_summary: Adopters must be at least 15 years older than the child. A court may allow a smaller gap for good reasons, such as siblings.
notes: Service-public page checked 8 June 2026.

rule_summary: Approval allows an age gap of no more than 50 years between the youngest adopter and the youngest child.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026. Search results say the law of 21 February 2022 added this rule.

rule_summary: An information meeting is part of the approval process. Within 2 months of the first letter, the council sends a guide and offers meetings.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026. The first step is a simple letter to the council president.

rule_summary: The council must decide within 9 months of the day the applicant confirms the request by registered letter.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: The child welfare service (ASE) carries out a social and a psychological assessment. Assessors meet the applicant at least twice.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026. Applicants may ask for a second assessment by different people and may be heard by the approval committee.

rule_summary: Applicants send a medical certificate under 3 months old from an approved doctor. It covers everyone living in the home.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: Applicants send proof of their income. The page sets no minimum income.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: Since 1 February 2026, adoption applicants need a certificate of good character under 6 months old. Applicants also send bulletin n°3 of their criminal record.
notes: News item published 4 February 2026. Without the certificate the council cannot examine the request.

rule_summary: Adoption approval lasts 5 years. It covers one adoption procedure only.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: Each year, approved applicants confirm they still wish to adopt. They send a sworn statement and a new certificate of good character.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026. The council holds an update interview by the end of the second year.

rule_summary: After a refusal or withdrawal of approval, the applicant must wait 30 months before applying again.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: A refusal can be challenged with the council within 2 months, or taken straight to the administrative court.
legal_citation: Code de justice administrative R421-1 to R421-7
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: An approval stays valid after a move to another département. The person must declare the new address by registered letter within 2 months.
notes: Service-public page checked by the site on 22 July 2026.

rule_summary: Full adoption (adoption plénière) is, in principle, for children under 15. The child must have lived with the adopters for at least 6 months.
notes: Service-public page checked 8 June 2026. Some exceptions allow full adoption up to 21.

rule_summary: A child over 13 must consent to their adoption before a notary.
notes: Service-public page checked 8 June 2026.

rule_summary: A court application to adopt needs a €50 tax stamp, unless the applicant gets legal aid.
notes: Service-public page checked 8 June 2026. Approval by the council has no fee on the pages read.

rule_summary: For adoption from abroad, applicants use the State agency, an authorised adoption body (OAA) or, in some cases, apply alone. The foreign ministry approves each body's fees.
notes: Ministry page updated 30 July 2026. It lists 6 active bodies. Approved running cost fees range from €2,135 to €4,380.

rule_summary: In Gironde, pay for one child was €2,027.10 gross a month from 1 January 2024. Two children: €2,644.55. Three children: €3,762.95.
notes: Gironde council page. Maintenance allowances are paid on top.

rule_summary: Gironde's page still describes 300 hours of training: 60 hours before the first child and 240 hours within 3 years.
notes: The national figures rose in 2025 to 100 and 420 hours.

rule_summary: In Gironde, the approval form is given out only at a monthly information meeting in Bordeaux.
notes: Gironde council page.

rule_summary: In Haute-Vienne, the information meetings before approval are compulsory. The approval file is handed out there.
notes: Haute-Vienne council page.

rule_summary: In Deux-Sèvres, a refused applicant can ask within 2 months to meet the PMI service to learn why.
notes: Deux-Sèvres council page.

rule_summary: In Loire-Atlantique, pay for one child is €1,960 gross a month, and €3,005 for two.
notes: Loire-Atlantique council page. It says pay during training rose from €576 to €1,520 gross.

rule_summary: In Loire-Atlantique, carers take a 100-hour course before the first child, then 420 hours of training within 3 years.
notes: Loire-Atlantique council page. It matches the 2025 national figures.

rule_summary: In Loire-Atlantique, the applicant and everyone over 13 living in the home must provide a certificate of good character.
notes: Loire-Atlantique council page. Employers ask for a certificate under 6 months old.

rule_summary: Paris pays at least the SMIC for the first child, €1,801.80 gross a month at 1 January 2025. Each extra child adds at least 70 hours of SMIC.
notes: Ville de Paris page updated 10 December 2025.

rule_summary: Paris carers get at least 35 days of paid leave a year.
notes: Ville de Paris page updated 10 December 2025. Carers in some areas get more days.

rule_summary: Paris says no training is needed for approval. After recruitment, carers take a 100-hour course and 420 hours of initial training.
notes: Ville de Paris page updated 10 December 2025.

rule_summary: In the Yvelines, a €1,000 bonus is paid when the first child arrives.
notes: From the council's recruitment site, seen in search results. The site refused our program.

rule_summary: In Eure-et-Loir, first-time applicants must attend an information meeting (RIPA) before collecting or filing an approval file.
notes: Eure-et-Loir online services page. Booking is compulsory, and a partner who comes must book too.

rule_summary: In the Var, the information meeting is optional. Applicants who attend send proof of attendance with their file.
notes: Var council page.

rule_summary: In Vaucluse, pay starts at €2,000 net a month for one child.
notes: Net, not gross. Seen in search results; the site refused our program.

rule_summary: In the Métropole de Lyon, the information meeting is compulsory before asking the PMI service for approval.
notes: Toodego is the Métropole's online services site.

rule_summary: In Puy-de-Dôme, gross pay for one child was €1,823.07 a month from 1 January 2026.
notes: Seen in search results; the site showed our program a bot check.

rule_summary: Puy-de-Dôme asks carers to have a driving licence and a car.
notes: Several other councils, such as Moselle, Somme and Vaucluse, ask the same in search results.

rule_summary: In Hérault, pay for one child in full-time care is €1,827.04 a month. Two children: €2,908.84. Three children: €3,990.64.
notes: Hérault council page. The page does not say whether the amounts are gross.

rule_summary: In Hérault, carers get €20 per child per day of presence for daily costs.
notes: Hérault council page.

rule_summary: In Hérault, carers get a yearly bonus of €600 to €1,400.
notes: Hérault council page. The value is the lowest amount.

rule_summary: In the Gard, the information meeting is not compulsory but is strongly advised.
notes: Seen in search results; the site refused our program.

rule_summary: In Haute-Garonne, applicants book the information meeting (RIPA) online. It can be in person or by video.
notes: Haute-Garonne online form page. A place is confirmed later by email.

rule_summary: In Morbihan, pay ranges from €1,767 a month for one young person to €3,722 for three in full-time care.
notes: Seen in search results; the site closed the connection to our program.

rule_summary: In the Oise, the council offers up to €10,000 to help carers adapt their home.
notes: Seen in search results; the site refused our program. The value is the maximum.

rule_summary: In the Oise, carers take 100 hours of training when recruited and 420 hours within 3 years.
notes: Seen in search results; the site refused our program.

rule_summary: In Bas-Rhin, the information meeting is compulsory for every approval request. The approval file is given out at the meeting.
notes: Collectivité européenne d'Alsace page seen in search results; the site closed the connection to our program.
